html:
The Uru are an Indigenous people of the Andean high plateau, living along the waters of Lake Titicaca, the Desaguadero River and Lake Poopó in Bolivia and Peru.

They lived from the lakes, fishing, hunting water birds and gathering reeds, and some lived on floating islands built of totora reeds. The Uros islands near Puno in Peru are the best known today. The Aymara and the Inca treated the Uru as the lowest people of the plateau, and Inca and Spanish tax lists counted them apart. In the 1500s they were a large share of the people around the lakes.

Most Uru later shifted to speaking Aymara. Their own languages, of the Uru-Chipaya family, survive mainly among the Chipaya of Oruro. Their neighbours included the Aymara lordships such as Killaka Asanajaqi, and Lake Titicaca had earlier been the heart of Tiwanaku.
sum: The Uru are an Indigenous people of the Andean high plateau, living along the waters of Lake Titicaca, the Desaguadero River and Lake Poopó in Bolivia and Peru.
